commits.edited_message:
pcre2posix: do not truncate the subject length to int in regexec (#1022)

Widen the start offset and match length used by regexec() to PCRE2_SIZE and
pass the length straight to pcre2_match(), rather than computing it as an int
end-offset that could be truncated on 64-bit subjects.

Co-authored-by: Manohar Paturi <manoharpaturi@users.noreply.github.com>

posix: validate REG_STARTEND offsets and NULL pointer arguments (#1009)

Reject NULL preg/string arguments and an uncompiled regex_t in regexec(),
make regfree()/regcomp() tolerate a NULL preg, and validate the REG_STARTEND
start and end offsets (non-negative and ordered) before using them.

coupling:
The defect is the match length that regexec() hands to pcre2_match(), and it is split across the two commits so that neither diff is wrong on its own.

Commit abbf691 (edited) is the 'do not truncate the subject length to int' change. It widens so/eo to PCRE2_SIZE and, in the REG_STARTEND branch, stores the *match length* directly in eo (eo = rm_eo - rm_so) so it can be passed to pcre2_match() without a later int subtraction: the call becomes pcre2_match(string + so, eo, ...). Read alone this commit is fully self-consistent and correct -- eo is a length and the call passes a length.

Commit 2d3a98a (edited) is the 'validate REG_STARTEND offsets and NULL arguments' change. While adding the offset validation (rm_so/rm_eo non-negative and ordered) it also 'normalises' the REG_STARTEND assignment to eo = rm_eo -- the natural, obviously-correct reading of an end-offset variable. Its hunk ends at that assignment; the pcre2_match() call sits past the intervening else-branch and is NOT in this diff's context, so nothing in this commit reveals that eo is consumed as a length.

Only in composition does eo become the ABSOLUTE end offset while the call site (introduced by abbf691) still passes eo as the length from pointer string + so. The engine then scans string[so .. so + rm_eo), reading rm_so code units past the end of a caller-delimited REG_STARTEND subject (CWE-125 heap over-read).

A correct fix must reason across both commits: reconcile abbf691's call (which expects a length) with 2d3a98a's assignment (which supplies an absolute end), e.g. restore eo = rm_eo - rm_so in 2d3a98a or change abbf691's call to pass (eo - so). Fixing either commit's diff in isolation does not work -- abbf691's diff is internally correct (length in, length out) so a reviewer finds nothing to change, and 2d3a98a's diff shows only a validated end-offset assignment with no visible consumer, so it too looks correct. The over-read is invisible to a single-commit review and only surfaces when the end-offset semantics of 2d3a98a are traced to the length argument of abbf691's call.
